primitives.meaning: a payment system stating that the attempt failed, with whatever reason it gave
entryFilters: the obligation is still outstanding in the system of record
the failure class is established from the provider's own response - temporary, customer-fixable, or declined with or without a usable reason - before anything is retried or said
no recovery instance is already open for this obligation; a second failure on the same obligation is an event inside the open instance (GLB-19)
the relationship has not been terminated
hard gates (GLB-31) permit obligation communication to this person - a closed account still receives it, a fraud or security hold does not

primitives.does: Classify the failure into the class the provider actually reported: temporary, insufficient funds, invalid method, expired method, authentication required, provider failure, policy decline, or unknown reason. A decline reason is never invented - telling someone their card had insufficient funds when the provider said only 'do not honour' is a checkable falsehood that sends them to fix the wrong thing

primitives.asks: What kind of failure was it?

branches.label: Transient, safe to retry
branches.test: a temporary condition or a provider-side failure, with the same idempotency key still valid

branches.label: The customer can fix it
branches.test: insufficient funds, an invalid or expired method, or an authentication that was not completed

branches.label: Declined, or no usable reason given
branches.test: a policy decline, or a decline whose reason cannot be turned into an instruction

primitives.does: Retry within the bounded policy, using the same idempotency key so that a first attempt which did land can be absorbed rather than repeated

primitives.key: the failed attempt's own idempotency key - the same key, so a first attempt that did land is absorbed rather than repeated

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the person has an active session in the product - the corrective action is a form, and the shortest route to it is inside the product
no active session, or the instruction and its link have to survive until the person can act

primitives.purpose: Name the exact corrective action - update the method, complete the authentication, choose another method - and what is owed. Provider risk detail and internal decline codes are never shown.
primitives.brief: Request the exact corrective action - update the method, complete the authentication, choose another method. Naming what to fix is the whole value of the classification, and a generic notice that payment failed makes the person guess. Provider risk detail and internal decline codes are not exposed

mustNotClaim: the reason the provider gave, beyond its class
that the obligation is waived, reduced or extended

primitives.asks: Is an alternative valid payment route available, and whose decision is it?

branches.label: A defined fallback the system may use
branches.test: another stored method exists and standing authority already covers charging it without asking again

branches.label: The customer has to choose or authorise one
branches.test: an alternative exists but no standing authority covers it, so using it would be charging a method they did not pick

branches.label: Nothing further to offer
branches.test: no alternative route is available or permitted

primitives.does: Charge the authorised alternative route as a new attempt with its own identifiers. Reached either because standing authority already covered it or because the customer selected it - in both cases the authority to use this method exists before it is used

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the person has an active session in the product - the corrective action is a form, and the shortest route to it is inside the product
no active session, or the instruction and its link have to survive until the person can act

primitives.purpose: Put the available alternative methods in front of the customer and ask which to use, stating that the obligation stands either way. Choosing a payment method is theirs to make.
primitives.brief: Put the available alternatives in front of the customer and ask which to use, stating that the obligation stands either way. Choosing a payment method is theirs to make; an internal action that quietly picks one is a charge they did not authorise

mustNotClaim: that a method was chosen for them

primitives.asks: Is a reminder still useful, and is there a consequence to name?

branches.label: Consequence ahead, obligation open
branches.test: the obligation is still outstanding, the method is still invalid, and an asserted consequence date lies ahead

branches.label: Nothing to add
branches.test: no consequence date exists, or the situation has not changed in a way a reminder would change

primitives.purpose: One reminder naming the consequence and its date, with the same corrective action. It is not repeated.
primitives.brief: Say once that the consequence is approaching and when, and repeat the same corrective action. One notice - a second one is a recovery sequence, not a reminder

primitives.asks: The obligation is unpaid after the recovery window - what does policy apply?

branches.label: Grace period
branches.test: policy continues limited service while the obligation remains unresolved

branches.label: Overdue tracking
branches.test: the obligation moves to an overdue operational state without immediate consequence

branches.label: Access restriction
branches.test: policy restricts capability while the obligation is unpaid

primitives.on: an unpaid obligation entering a grace period
carries: the obligation and the recovery already attempted
the explicit fact that the commercial relationship has not ended - this is a payment problem
the obligation, its due date and the failure history against it

primitives.on: policy restricting capability while an obligation is unpaid
carries: the obligation, so restoring access has something to check against
